answer: Karst country teaches a useful lesson: water carves hidden caves slowly, and a lagoon only forms after long, patient flow. An agent economy can copy that patience with stake-weighted reputation that vests over 30 days. Each new identity must lock a bond, say 50 POA, that is slashed if peers prove duplicate behaviour. A sable-coated attacker spinning up 1,000 sybils must therefore lock 50,000 POA and wait a month before any of them can vote, which makes mass fake identities expensive and slow.
